note: The rule's own example made real: box 2 alone, the crossing from box 1 with the two crossing notes lit, the same shapes moved to C, then improvising across both. Each block changes position, key or task.

exercise.title: Join boxes 1 and 2
exercise.focus: Minor pentatonic · boxes 1 → 2 · A then C
exercise.why: Joining boxes turns five separate shapes into one neck you can move along mid-phrase.

sections.text: Players get stuck in box 1 because they never practise leaving it; one slide on the G string is the door to box 2.
Play box 2 of A minor pentatonic up and down at 70, one note per click. It starts at the 7th fret; the {{1}} sits on the D and B strings.

Climb box 1 from the low A. On the G string, play {{4}} (D, 7th fret) with your ring finger and slide it up to {{5}} (E, 9th fret); finish the climb in box 2. Come back down the same way, sliding from {{5}} to {{4}}. Done when the slide lands in time, four runs in a row.
Move everything up three frets: C minor pentatonic, box 1 at the 8th fret. Same crossing, same fingers, sliding from {{4}} (F) to {{5}} (G) on the G string.
Press Play and improvise over Cm7 and Fm7 using both boxes. Cross at least once per phrase. Land on {{c}} when Cm7 comes round and on {{f}} when Fm7 does.
